mainTopic: Flour or incense caught between the fingers in קמיצה and חפינה, and רב פפא's unresolved questions about unusual ways of taking a handful
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about how a כהן takes the קומץ from a fried מנחה, and the ברייתא calls this the hardest עבודה in the מקדש. The גמרא corrects the wording to 'one of the hardest,' since מליקה and חפינה are also very hard. Next, רבי יהושע בן עוזאה asks about the flour caught between the fingers of the קומץ. רב פפא narrows the question to the middle zone, and the ruling is that this flour is a ספק. רבי חנינא says to burn the definite קומץ first and the doubtful flour afterward, so the שירים are not reduced before the קומץ is burned. The גמרא objects that burning possible שירים violates בל תקטירו. It answers that the flour is burned as fuel, following רבי אליעזר, and that ideally fat-fingered כהנים do the קמיצה so no doubt arises at all. After a סימן, רב פפא asks the same in-between question about the כהן גדול's handfuls of קטורת on יום כיפור, recast as whether the 'taking' and the 'bringing' must match. He then asks about unusual ways of doing קמיצה and חפינה, and all of these questions end in תיקו. The amud closes as another dilemma begins, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Smoothing the קומץ for fried מנחות, the hardest עבודה in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends its description of קמיצה. For a מנחת מחבת or מנחת מרחשת, the כהן wipes off extra flour with his thumb on top and his little finger on the bottom. It calls this the hardest עבודה in the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a pan-offering and a deep-pot offering, he wipes off with his thumb on top and with his little finger on the bottom. And this is the hardest service in the Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא that teaches exactly how the כהן takes the handful. Here it covers the fried מנחות and then praises this task as the hardest job in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fried מנחה is crumbly and hard, so pieces stick out of the closed hand. The כהן must trim the excess very precisely, using his thumb above and his little finger below, so that the handful is exactly a full handful and no more. That precision is why the ברייתא calls it the hardest עבודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A flat pan; a מנחה fried in a shallow pan
A deep pot; a מנחה fried in a deep vessel
Wipes off or levels the excess

phrases.english: And with a pan-offering and a deep-pot offering,
phrases.notes: These are fried, so the flour is hard and sticks out of the hand.

phrases.english: he wipes off with his thumb from above,
and with his little finger from below.
And this is the difficult service in the Temple.
phrases.notes: Read literally, it sounds like 'THE single hardest service.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא describing the method of קמיצה, which began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For fried מנחות the כהן trims the excess with his thumb above and his little finger below. קמיצה is called the hardest עבודה in the מקדש.

steps.title: Challenge: other services are also extremely hard
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether קמיצה is really the only hardest service. מליקה and חפינה are also known to be very difficult.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one and nothing else? But there is pinching (מליקה), and there is scooping the incense (חפינה)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's wording. If קמיצה is 'the' hardest service, what about מליקה and חפינה, which are also famously hard?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack targets the ברייתא's exclusive phrasing ('this is THE hard service'). מליקה means killing a bird with the fingernail. חפינה is the כהן גדול scooping two handfuls of קטורת on יום כיפור. Both require great skill, so calling קמיצה uniquely hardest seems inaccurate.

keyTerms.meaning: Killing a bird-offering by nipping its neck with the fingernail
Scooping handfuls of קטורת (done by the כהן גדול on יום כיפור)

phrases.english: This is it, and nothing else?
But there is pinching (of birds),
and there is scooping (of incense)!

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ הִיא וְתוּ לָא? וְהָא אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last line of the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'וְזוֹ הִיא עֲבוֹדָה קָשָׁה שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ', read as exclusive
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Other services (מליקה, חפינה) are equally difficult, so קמיצה cannot be the single hardest.

steps.title: Correction: it is one of the hardest services
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: קמיצה is one of the hardest services, not the only one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: this is one of the difficult services in the Temple.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by correcting the reading of the ברייתא. קמיצה belongs to a group of very hard services.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fix is small but exact: 'עבודה קשה' becomes 'מעבודות קשות', meaning 'from among the hard services.' Now קמיצה, מליקה and חפינה can all be counted as extremely difficult without any contradiction.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: זוֹ הִיא מֵעֲבוֹדוֹת קָשׁוֹת שֶׁבַּמִּקְדָּשׁ.
phrases.english: Rather: this is one of the difficult services in the Temple.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading or correcting the wording of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא calls קמיצה the single hardest service.
steps.terutzMaskana: קמיצה is one of several hardest services, alongside מליקה and חפינה.

steps.title: The question about flour between the fingers
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reports that רבי יהושע בן עוזאה asked about the flour lodged between the fingers of the handful. Does it count as the קומץ or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי יהושע בן עוזאה asked: What is the status of the flour in between, of his full handful?
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. When the כהן closes his hand, some flour gets caught between his fingers, and the question is whether that flour is part of the קומץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every grain of the מנחה must be either קומץ, which is burned on the מזבח, or שירים, the remainder eaten by the כהנים. Flour wedged between the fingers is in a gray zone, and its status determines what may be done with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked or raised a question (often an unresolved halachic doubt)
The in-between area (here, between the fingers)
What is it? What is the law?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said,
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Uza'a asked:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הַבֵּינַיִם שֶׁל מְלֹא קוּמְצוֹ, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: The in-between flour of his full handful, what is its status?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, בָּעֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן עוּזָּאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Stays with קמיצה but opens a new question about the edges of the handful.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the flour between the fingers considered part of the קומץ or part of the שירים?

steps.title: רב פפא narrows the question to the middle zone
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says flour toward the inside of the hand is surely קומץ, and flour toward the outside is surely שירים. The question is only about the flour in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: About the inner flour, don't ask, because it is certainly קומץ. About the outer flour, don't ask, because it is certainly שירים. Where you should ask is about the flour right in between: what is it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא clarifies exactly what the question is about. He removes the clear cases so that only the truly doubtful middle remains, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flour between the fingers sits on a range. The part deep inside, near the palm, is clearly held in the fist, so it is קומץ. The part at the outer edge is clearly outside the hand, so it is שירים. Only the strip in the middle of the finger-gap is truly unclear.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not ask about it (it is obvious)
The remainder of the מנחה after the קומץ is taken
That which is right in the middle

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
About the inner flour, do not ask,
because it is certainly handful.
About the outer flour, do not ask,
because it is certainly remainder.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ דְּבֵינֵי בֵּינֵי מַאי.
phrases.english: Where you should ask is about the flour right in between: what is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact scope of the question from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Inner flour is definitely קומץ, outer flour is definitely שירים, and only the middle flour is in question.

steps.title: The answer: the in-between flour is a ספק
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן עוזאה later resolved his own question: the middle flour has doubtful status.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: רבי יהושע בן עוזאה later resolved it: the in-between flour is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The same חכם who asked the question answers it. The middle flour has no clear status, so it must be treated as a ספק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the 'answer' is not a decision that the flour is קומץ or that it is שירים. Instead, it rules that the status cannot be determined, so we must act in a way that works either way. This leads directly to the practical question in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think 'resolved' means he decided the flour is קומץ or שירים. He resolved that it stays a ספק, and we must be strict both ways.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Yehoshua ben Uza'a then resolved it:
The in-between flour is doubtful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question as narrowed in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The middle flour has doubtful status and is treated as a ספק.

steps.title: So what does the כהן actually do?
steps.stepSummary: Since the middle flour is a ספק, the גמרא asks how the כהן should handle it in practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does he act?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move: once the flour is a ספק, how does the כהן perform the service correctly?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ספק status creates a practical problem. The flour cannot simply be thrown away or eaten, because it might be קומץ that must be burned. The question asks for a procedure that is safe either way.

keyTerms.meaning: How does he act? (asks for practical procedure)

phrases.english: How does he act?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the ספק ruling and asks for its practical application.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the correct procedure for burning the קומץ together with the doubtful in-between flour?

steps.title: רבי חנינא: burn the definite קומץ first
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא rules that the כהן burns the certain קומץ alone first, and only afterward burns the doubtful in-between flour.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: He burns the קומץ by itself first, and afterward the in-between flour.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives the practical order of burning. The sure קומץ goes first, and the doubtful flour goes second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is the key. The doubtful flour is still burned, in case it is truly קומץ, but only after the definite קומץ has already been offered. The next step explains why this order matters.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
He burns the handful by itself first,
and afterward the in-between flour.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַקְטִיר קוֹמֶץ לְחוֹדֵיהּ תְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the practical question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Burn the certain קומץ first, then the doubtful in-between flour.

steps.title: Why the order matters: reduced שירים disqualify the קומץ
steps.stepSummary: If the doubtful flour were burned first and turned out to be שירים, the שירים would have shrunk before the קומץ was burned. A known rule (אמר מר) says the קומץ may not be burned on account of such reduced שירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because if you say to burn the in-between flour first, maybe it is שירים, and then they become שירים that were reduced between the taking of the handful and the burning. And the Master said: For שירים that were reduced between the taking and the burning, we do not burn the קומץ on their account.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי חנינא's order and backs it up with an established rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The burning of the קומץ is what permits the שירים, so the שירים must still be whole at the moment the קומץ is burned. If the כהן burned the doubtful flour first and it was really שירים, he would have reduced the שירים before the קומץ went up, and that disqualifies the burning. Burning the definite קומץ first avoids this risk entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: Between taking the handful and burning it
And the Master said (quotes an established teaching)

steps.whatToRemember: The in-between flour is a ספק. The כהן burns the definite קומץ first, and only then the doubtful flour, because שירים that shrink before the קומץ is burned disqualify the burning of the קומץ.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how a ספק is handled in עבודה: you choose an order that stays valid whichever way the doubt turns out.

phrases.english: For if you say the in-between flour first,
perhaps it is remainder,
and then they become remainders
that were reduced between taking the handful and burning,
and the Master said:
Remainders that were reduced between taking the handful and burning,
we do not burn the handful on their account.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning and source support for רבי חנינא's order.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's ruling that the definite קומץ must be burned before the in-between flour
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of 'מר': שירים that were reduced between קמיצה and הקטרה disqualify the burning of the קומץ on their account.

steps.title: Burning the doubtful flour afterward still risks a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חנינא. Even if the doubtful flour is burned after the קומץ, it might be שירים, and burning שירים violates בל תקטירו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, now too we should apply the rule: anything that has a part going to the fire of the מזבח falls under the prohibition 'do not burn.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי חנינא's solution from Step 8. Burning the doubtful flour second still does not make the problem go away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that once part of a מנחה (the קומץ) is burned on the מזבח, burning any other part of it (the שירים) is forbidden. The in-between flour might be שירים. So burning it at any time, even after the קומץ, could violate בל תקטירו.

keyTerms.meaning: If so (introduces a challenge built on what was just said)
Anything that has a part going to the fire of the altar
The prohibition 'do not burn' (burning non-designated parts on the altar)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 9 solved only an ordering problem: the שירים must not be reduced before the קומץ is burned. This step raises a completely separate problem. Burning possible שירים on the מזבח at all may be forbidden.

phrases.english: If so, now too
let us apply here [the rule]:
whatever has a part of it going to the fire —
is subject to 'do not burn.'
phrases.notes: The rest of it may not be burned on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, הַשְׁתָּא נָמֵי אִיקְּרִי כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the procedure from Step 8 that Step 9 supported.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנינא's instruction to burn the doubtful flour after the קומץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The doubtful flour may be שירים. Burning שירים violates בל תקטירו regardless of the order.

steps.title: The doubtful flour is burned as fuel, like רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי answers that the כהן burns the doubtful flour as wood (fuel), not as an offering. This follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה, son of רבי שמעון בן פזי, said: he burns it as wood, following רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא answers the challenge. The כהן burns the in-between flour as fuel for the fire, not as part of the offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בל תקטירו forbids burning something as an offering. If the flour is burned only as fuel (לשום עצים), it is not being offered, so there is no violation. This works only according to רבי אליעזר's view.

keyTerms.meaning: For the purpose of wood, as fuel only
The תנא who permits burning forbidden items as fuel

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi, said:
that he burns it as wood,
in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Recharacterizes the act: burning as fuel rather than as an offering
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning the doubtful flour counts as offering possible שירים, which violates בל תקטירו.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is burned only as fuel, which רבי אליעזר permits.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing רבי אליעזר permits burning as fuel
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי אליעזר. The פסוק forbids bringing such items 'for a sweet savor,' but they may be brought up as wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אליעזר says, 'for a sweet savor' you may not bring it up, but you may bring it up as wood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source for רבי אליעזר's view, which backs up the answer in Step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר reads the words 'לריח ניחוח' closely. The פסוק forbids only offering the item as a pleasing offering. Burning it purely as fuel is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught (in a ברייתא)
For a sweet savor, meaning as a pleasing offering

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
'for a sweet savor' you may not bring it up,
phrases.notes: ויקרא ב:יב, about leaven and honey.

phrases.english: but you may bring it up as wood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the answer in Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That burning לשום עצים is permitted according to רבי אליעזר

steps.title: What about the רבנן, who disagree with רבי אליעזר?
steps.stepSummary: The fuel answer works only for רבי אליעזר. The רבנן reject it, so what would they say?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי אליעזר, but according to the רבנן, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the answer covers only one opinion. It asks how the problem is solved according to the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן do not allow burning forbidden items even as fuel. According to them, the original problem of בל תקטירו comes back.

phrases.english: This works well according to Rabbi Eliezer,
but according to the Rabbis, what can be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, אֶלָּא לְרַבָּנַן מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the answer from Step 11 to one opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן reject burning as fuel, so the answer fails according to them.

steps.title: Fat כהנים take the קומץ
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי answers that the קמיצה is done by כהנים with fleshy fingers. Their fingers close tightly, so no in-between flour is left.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said: fat כהנים take the handful.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי gives a practical solution for the רבנן. Avoid creating the doubt in the first place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Thick fingers press against each other and leave no gaps. With no in-between flour, there is no doubtful flour to deal with, and the question of בל תקטירו never comes up.

phrases.english: Rav Mari said: that fat [priests] take the handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical avoidance: the doubtful case is prevented from arising
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to the רבנן, the doubtful flour cannot be burned at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Fat-fingered כהנים do the קמיצה, so no doubtful flour exists.

steps.title: Even רבי אליעזר prefers fat כהנים from the start
steps.stepSummary: Now that the solution of fat כהנים exists, even רבי אליעזר would use it לכתחילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have come to this, even according to רבי אליעזר, fat כהנים should take the handful from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up this section. The fat-כהנים solution is the preferred approach for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's fuel option is only a fallback for when the doubt already exists. Ideally (לכתחילה), even he would avoid creating the doubt at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have arrived at this
From the start, the ideal way

steps.whatToRemember: The in-between flour is a ספק. The ideal solution is to have fat-fingered כהנים do the קמיצה so that no doubt ever arises. רבי אליעזר also allows burning such flour as fuel after the fact.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this,
according to Rabbi Eliezer too, from the start,
fat [priests] should take the handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רב מרי's answer to רבי אליעזר as well.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For all opinions, fat-fingered כהנים should do the קמיצה לכתחילה.

steps.title: Memory aid for רב פפא's upcoming questions
steps.stepSummary: A סימן (memory aid) lists key words from the series of questions רב פפא is about to ask.
steps.simpleTranslation: In-between, 'פשט' (perhaps 'obvious' or 'spread out'), pressed flat, scattered, intended, with his fellow's handful: this is a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. It gives a list of code words to help remember the questions that come next. It does not argue anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one of רב פפא's coming statements or questions. 'בין הבינים' is his question about the in-between of the קטורת handfuls, which starts right away in the next step. 'פשט' most likely points to his 'פשיטא לי' statements about normal קמיצה and חפינה. The rest point to questions that continue onto the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: The in-between (what is between the fingers)
Taking a double handful (used for the קטורת)

phrases.english: (In-between, 'obvious,' pressed flat,
scattered, intended,
with his fellow's handful — a mnemonic).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section after the conclusion in Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. It is a mnemonic for the coming questions.

steps.title: What about the in-between of the כהן גדול's handfuls?
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks about the קטורת caught between the fingers when the כהן גדול takes his double handfuls (מלא חפניו) on יום כיפור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: what is the law of the in-between of 'his full handfuls'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא moves the same question over to the קטורת of יום כיפור. Does the incense between the fingers count as part of the handful?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the question was about the קומץ of a מנחה. Now it is about the חפינה of קטורת, which the תורה describes as 'מלא חפניו.'

keyTerms.meaning: His full handfuls (the כהן גדול's קטורת on יום כיפור)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa raised a dilemma:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הַבֵּינַיִם שֶׁל מְלֹא חׇפְנָיו מַהוּ?
phrases.english: The in-between of 'his full handfuls' — what is [the law]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first question listed in the mnemonic of Step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the incense between the fingers counts as part of מלא חפניו

steps.title: What is the question? It should be the same as the קומץ
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב פפא's doubt even is. If 'מלא' is learned from 'מלא' of the מנחה, the case is identical to the one already discussed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his question? If he learns 'full' from 'full' from there, this is the same as that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the question itself. It argues that the answer should already be known from the מנחה case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מלא' appear by the קומץ and by the קטורת, linking the two through a גזירה שוה. If the link holds, the in-between incense should have the same status as the in-between flour. So why ask?

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as that

phrases.english: What is his dilemma?
If he derives 'full' from 'full' from there —
phrases.notes: From the קומץ of the מנחה.

phrases.english: this is the same as that!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for רב פפא's question in Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The basis of רב פפא's dilemma
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גזירה שוה of מלא/מלא makes the קטורת case identical to the קומץ case, so there should be nothing new to ask.

steps.title: What רב פפא was really asking: matching the taking and the bringing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers its own challenge by rewording רב פפא's doubt. Is it enough that full handfuls were brought, or must the 'taking' and 'bringing' match exactly? The question stays unresolved (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: This is how רב פפא asked it: Do we only need 'his hands full… and bring,' and that happened here? Or perhaps we need 'and he shall take… and he shall bring' to match, and that did not happen here? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the last step. It shows that רב פפא's question was a different one from the case of the מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side 1: the פסוק only requires the כהן גדול to bring full handfuls, and he did. Side 2: the פסוק links 'וְלָקַח' to 'וְהֵבִיא', so whatever he brings must be what he meant to take. The incense stuck between his fingers was never intentionally taken, so that requirement may be missing. Because the question is about the link between taking and bringing, it is not the same as the מנחה case.

keyTerms.meaning: it is there / it is not there
and he shall bring (inside the פרוכת)
let it stand; the question is left unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume this is the same doubt as the in-between flour of the מנחה (steps 4–6). רב פפא is not asking whether the in-between incense is part of the handful. He is asking whether the incense that is brought must match the incense that was intentionally taken.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked it like this:
Do we require only "his hands full… and bring"?
And that is present here.
Or perhaps we require "and he shall take… and he shall bring" to match?
phrases.notes: Whatever is brought must be what he meant to take.

phrases.english: And that is missing here?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 18 by rewording רב פפא's question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rewording the question so it is about a different issue
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's question seemed to be the same as the מנחה case about 'מלא'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The question is whether 'וְלָקַח' and 'וְהֵבִיא' must match, which is a new issue. It remains תיקו.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תיקו: it is unresolved whether the extra incense between the fingers is valid.

steps.title: The normal way of taking a handful is obviously correct
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא states that קמיצה done the way people normally grab a handful is clearly valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is obvious to me that 'his handful' means the way people usually take a handful.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sets a clear starting point for the קמיצה of a מנחה. This prepares the questions in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal grab, with the fingers pointing down into the flour, is the standard way and is clearly fine. Starting from this obvious case lets רב פפא next ask about less normal ways of grabbing.

keyTerms.meaning: his handful (the קמיצה of a מנחה)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is obvious to me
that "his handful" means the way people take a handful.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of questions about how קמיצה is done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normal קמיצה, the way people usually grab, is valid.

steps.title: Questions about unusual ways of taking a handful
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks about three unusual ways of doing קמיצה. None of them is answered (תיקו).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: If he took the handful with his fingertips, what is the law? If he took it from below going up, what is the law? If he took it from the sides, what is the law? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks whether three unusual grabbing methods still count as קמיצה. The גמרא cannot decide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fingertips: he puts his palm in and pulls the flour in with his fingers. Below to above: the back of his hand faces down and his fingers sweep the flour up into his palm. From the sides: he moves his hand back and forth so flour gathers in his palm. The doubt each time is whether a method that is not the normal one is still valid.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If he took a handful with his fingertips, what is the law?
From below to above, what is the law?
From the sides, what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: קָמַץ בְּרָאשֵׁי אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the obvious normal case to unusual cases.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether non-standard methods of קמיצה are valid.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תיקו: all three cases are unresolved.

steps.title: The normal way of scooping with both hands is obviously correct
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא states that the כהן גדול's חפינה on יום כיפור, done the way people normally scoop with both hands, is clearly valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is obvious to me that 'his hands full' means the way people usually scoop with both hands.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sets the same kind of starting point for the חפינה of the קטורת. This prepares the next set of questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal way is to put the backs of both hands into the vessel and bring the hands together. This copies the structure of step 20, but now for the two-handed scoop of קטורת.

keyTerms.meaning: the way people scoop with both hands

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: It is obvious to me
that "his hands full" means the way people scoop with both hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: פְּשִׁיטָא לִי ״מְלֹא חׇפְנָיו״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 20, now applied to חפינה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Normal חפינה, the way people usually scoop, is valid.

steps.title: Questions about unusual ways of scooping with both hands
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks about four unusual ways of doing חפינה, including scooping with each hand separately and then joining the hands. All are left unresolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: If he scooped with his fingertips, what is the law? From below to above, what is the law? From the side, what is the law? If he scooped with this hand and with this hand and then brought them together, what is the law? Let it stand unresolved.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא repeats his three unusual methods for חפינה and adds a fourth case. The גמרא leaves all of them as תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first three cases match the קמיצה questions. The new fourth case: each hand scoops on its own and the hands are joined only afterward. The doubt is whether this counts as one two-handed scoop, since the hands were not scooping together.

keyTerms.meaning: with this hand and with this hand (separately)

steps.whatToRemember: The normal way of doing קמיצה and חפינה is clearly valid. Every unusual method רב פפא asks about, and also the question of incense stuck between the fingers, ends in תיקו.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If he scooped with his fingertips, what is the law?
From below to above, what is the law?
From the side, what is the law?
If he scooped with this hand and with this hand
and then brought them next to each other, what is the law?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: חָפַן בְּרָאשֵׁי אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the questions of step 21 to חפינה and adds a two-hands case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether non-standard methods of חפינה, including scooping with each hand separately, are valid.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: תיקו: all four cases are unresolved.

steps.title: Opening word of a new dilemma
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא uses the word בָּעֵי to signal that a new dilemma is about to be asked. The asker and the question appear on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another dilemma was raised (by):
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. The word בָּעֵי tells us that someone is about to ask a new question, but the question itself has not started yet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בָּעֵי is the standard opening formula for a בעיא, which is a real unknown question and not an attack on an earlier statement. Steps 21 and 23 ended in unanswered questions (תיקו) about unusual ways of doing קמיצה and חפינה, so this word opens another question in the same line of study. Do not guess the content yet. Wait for the next passage to name the asker and the case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He asked.' This is the opening formula for a dilemma (בעיא).
A real question of law that the גמרא does not know the answer to. It is not a challenge.
A related formula meaning 'he asked of him.' It is used when the question is put to a specific person.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read בָּעֵי as a קשיא (challenge). It means someone is truly asking because they do not know, not attacking an earlier statement.

phrases.english: He asked (raised a dilemma)
phrases.notes: This is a single word because it is the whole passage. The name of the asker comes right after, on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It follows the תיקו of step 23 and opens one more dilemma. The remaining code words of the mnemonic in step 16 (מחץ, פזר, חשב, בחפינת חבירו, and possibly פשט, unless it refers to the 'פשיטא לי' statements) have not been covered yet.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not yet stated. The actual question appears on the next amud.
